nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Eco-friendly consumer behavior
nodes.label: Eco-friendly consumer behavior

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Eco-friendly consumer behavior_qna_000
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What types of consumer-targeted policy instruments were investigated in the literature review?
nodes.answer: The literature review investigated four types of consumer-targeted policy instruments: market-based, information-based, regulatory, and nudging. These policy instruments aim to improve the sustainability of food systems by influencing consumer behaviour towards more environmentally friendly choices.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Eco-friendly consumer behavior_qna_001
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: How do market-based instruments differ from nudging instruments in influencing consumer behaviour?
nodes.answer: Market-based instruments, like taxes or subsidies affecting prices, use financial incentives to drive consumer behaviour, and are more intrusive than nudging instruments in promoting sustainability.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Eco-friendly consumer behavior_qna_002
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What impact did nudging and information-based instruments have on sustainable option choices?
nodes.answer: Nudging, like making the more sustainable burger the default choice, and information-based instruments have successfully increased sustainable option choices, as demonstrated by Prusak et al., 2,021 and Vlaeminck et al., 2014.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Eco-friendly consumer behavior_qna_003
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: How can menu design in restaurants influence consumer choices towards more responsible food options?
nodes.answer: Menu design in restaurants can influence consumer choices towards more responsible food options by using nudges such as highlighting healthy or sustainable dishes, using descriptive language to promote these options, and strategically placing them on the menu.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Eco-friendly consumer behavior_qna_004
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What are some strategies to improve consumers' judgments of foods in terms of environmental sustainability?
nodes.answer: Some strategies to improve consumers' judgments of foods in terms of environmental sustainability include providing clear and transparent information about the environmental impact of products, promoting sustainable production practices, and offering incentives for choosing environmentally friendly options.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Eco-friendly consumer behavior_qna_005
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What are some of the strategies mentioned in the text to promote cleaner and responsible consumption?
nodes.answer: Some strategies mentioned include using durable, quality goods, intensifying the use of goods, enabling repair, take back, and recycling, ensuring rental replaces product purchase, minimizing transport of goods, and reducing private vehicle kilometres travelled.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Eco-friendly consumer behavior_qna_006
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How can policymakers encourage sustainable consumption among low-income consumers?
nodes.answer: One strategy could be to make sustainable food options more affordable to eliminate the trade-off between price and sustainability. Policy instruments like subsidies for sustainable food production or tax incentives could help shift purchasing patterns towards sustainability, especially for low-income families.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Eco-friendly consumer behavior_qna_007
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How does Vermin et al. (2012) classify sustainable food consumers based on literature review?
nodes.answer: Vermin et al. (2012) classify sustainable food consumers into different classes based on a literature review, identifying various types of consumer attitudes and behaviours towards sustainable food consumption.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Eco-friendly consumer behavior_qna_008
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are some examples of companies collaborating with consumers to reduce waste according to the Harvard Business Review?
nodes.answer: Companies are actively working with consumers to reduce waste through various collaborative efforts, as highlighted in the Harvard Business Review.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Eco-friendly consumer behavior_qna_009
nodes.label: Science and Tech
nodes.question: What did Liu, Liu, and Mo (2020) examine regarding consumers' intention to purchase clothing made from recycled or organic materials?
nodes.answer: They examined how consumers' attitudes, subjective norms, perceived behavioural control, and moral norms influence their intention to purchase clothing made from recycled or organic materials.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Eco-friendly consumer behavior_qna_010
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How can bold and far-reaching business initiatives help companies reduce their dependence on consumerism?
nodes.answer: Bold business initiatives, even those contrary to companies' usual practices, can help reduce their reliance on consumerism by capturing new opportunities and mitigating emerging threats, ultimately reshaping their value proposition and competitive strategy.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Eco-friendly consumer behavior_qna_011
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How can companies like Patagonia contribute to changing consumers' mentality towards sustainability?
nodes.answer: Companies like Patagonia can contribute decisively to changing consumers' mentality towards sustainability through their value proposition and promotion, highlighting the positive impact of sustainability strategies.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Eco-friendly consumer behavior_qna_012
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: How does an individual exhibit direct green consumer behaviour, according to the text?
nodes.answer: An individual exhibits direct green consumer behaviour by purchasing green products, growing trees, reusing items, and avoiding the use of plastic bags.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Eco-friendly consumer behavior_qna_013
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does the concept of a green premium compare to a circular premium in consumer behaviour?
nodes.answer: The green premium and circular premium both reflect consumers' willingness to pay a higher price for environmentally friendly products, but the circular premium also includes considerations for recycled materials and ethical production practices.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Eco-friendly consumer behavior_qna_014
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: How can governments encourage the purchase of sustainable products among consumers?
nodes.answer: Governments can provide tax deductions or rebates to incentivize consumers to buy sustainable products, thus promoting eco-friendly choices.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Eco-friendly consumer behavior_qna_015
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Which nudging condition was the most effective at influencing participants towards selecting the most sustainable delivery option in the RCT?
nodes.answer: The default nudge was the most effective at steering participants towards selecting the most sustainable delivery option. This was followed by the medium- and low-informational nudging conditions in terms of influencing participants' choices towards sustainability.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Eco-friendly consumer behavior_qna_016
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why was the fully transparent informational nudge most effective in decreasing the likelihood of the least sustainable delivery choices?
nodes.answer: The fully transparent informational nudge triggered participants to think carefully about the options, leading to a decreased likelihood of choosing the least sustainable delivery choices.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Eco-friendly consumer behavior_qna_017
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What are the three stages of sustainable consumption behaviour (SCB) for plastics?
nodes.answer: SCB for plastics involves consumer choices along three stages: purchase, usage, and disposal of goods and services. In the purchasing phase, sustainable behaviour includes choosing plastics alternatives or more sustainable options. For example, Mangier et al. (2019) explored consumer willingness to pay a premium for recycled ocean plastics products.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Eco-friendly consumer behavior_qna_018
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: How can increasing personal responsibility and accountability among consumers help in plastic pollution mitigation?
nodes.answer: Increasing personal responsibility and accountability among consumers can help in plastic pollution mitigation by empowering them to take action. When consumers believe they have the power to effect change, they are more likely to make sustainable choices and reduce their contribution to plastic pollution.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Eco-friendly consumer behavior_qna_019
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: How can individuals in the Waste Conscious group be nudged towards more environmentally friendly behaviour?
nodes.answer: Individuals in the Waste Conscious group can be offered additional environmentally friendly options for purchase and disposal and be exposed to economic incentives, such as deposit-refund schemes or plastics taxes.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Eco-friendly consumer behavior_qna_020
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What are some strategies for promoting responsible environmental behaviour as discussed by Barr in their 2003 publication?
nodes.answer: In their 2003 publication, Barr discusses strategies for sustainability, including engaging citizens and promoting responsible environmental behaviour.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Eco-friendly consumer behavior_qna_021
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What strategies can be employed to promote repeat purchase behaviour for low-involvement products?
nodes.answer: Strategies to promote repeat purchase behaviour for low-involvement products may include implementing incentive programs, improving product design for durability, enhancing consumer education on the environmental impact of disposable products, and creating convenient systems for returning and reusing items.
